methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $1.0B total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
JetZero is a Series B-stage transportation company founded by Tom O'Leary and Mark Page that has raised over $1.0B to date. The transportation sector includes seven private peers at various stages (Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Arc Boats, The ePlane Company, and others), with no direct public comparables available. A narrow peer set at identical or adjacent stages and similar valuation tiers could not be established, limiting the applicability of median-based approaches.

Stage-progression methodology was applied as the primary triangulation method. Using total raised ($1.0B) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B-to-next-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $1.9B. This reflects the capital efficiency and de-risking expected between funding rounds at this stage.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $1.6B to $2.2B (median $1.9B), derived from sensitivity adjustments around the stage-progression result. Key uncertainties include the absence of same-stage transportation comparables to validate the 1.9x multiplier, execution risk on product development timelines typical of frontier transportation ventures, and market adoption trajectory. The single-method foundation and limited peer visibility at this valuation tier present material constraints on conviction. Additional data on round structure and investor composition would strengthen triangulation.
